description: We are Nexus+, a multidisciplinary team connecting aerospace engineering, chemical engineering, software development and AI. Like our name, we bring different fields together: understanding the physics and chemistry behind a problem, then building a clear, useful tool around it. We’re excited to use NASA’s open data to create solutions that make space exploration safer.
summary:
FireSafe SI is an AI-powered interactive dashboard that turns decades of NASA’s microgravity fire research into clear, usable safety insights. It combines an AI Research Assistant, which retrieves NASA findings and explains them with their sources, and an interactive 3D Module Risk Scanner, which lets users explore spacecraft components and investigate potential fire hazards.

It addresses the challenge by transforming scattered, hard-to-compare experimental data from NASA’s PSI database into answers engineers can act on: it summarizes investigations, compares their findings, and interprets them for fire safety, while clearly flagging what has never been tested, such as fire at Moon gravity.

Its focus is prevention. NASA’s Saffire experiments showed that toxic gases can build up before smoke is even detected, so in space, reacting is often too late. FireSafe SI helps engineers find the right evidence during design, before the mission. As humans prepare to live on the Moon and travel to Mars, where help is far away and habitats will run at higher oxygen levels, this knowledge can protect crews and bring them home.
details:
FireSafe SI – Making Space Exploration Safer

FireSafe SI is a platform we developed to make NASA’s fire-safety research easier to access, understand and use. NASA has conducted decades of experiments on how fire behaves in microgravity, but the amount of research available makes it difficult to find specific information and understand how it applies to future missions. We wanted to make this knowledge more accessible and useful.

Prevention first. In space, there’s no fire department and no exit. NASA’s Saffire experiments showed that in a spacecraft fire, toxic gases can build up before smoke is even detected. By the time an alarm rings, it may be too late to react. That’s why FireSafe SI is designed to act before the mission, not during the emergency: it helps engineers find the right evidence while they design spacecraft and habitats, so risky materials, conditions and design choices can be identified and avoided from the start.

Our platform brings together two main features. The first is an AI Research Assistant, where users ask questions about fire behavior in space, explore NASA experiments, and get explanations of scientific findings. It uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to retrieve relevant information from NASA research and the Claude API to generate answers grounded in that information, with sources. The second is an interactive 3D Module Risk Scanner, which lets users explore a spacecraft module, select components, and investigate potential fire hazards based on the research.

The main benefit of FireSafe SI is that it connects scientific research with practical design decisions. Instead of going through large amounts of technical documents, users can find, compare and understand the relevant evidence in an interactive way. The platform is mainly intended for aerospace engineers, researchers and space agencies, and it can also help students and anyone interested in space exploration.

We hope this project contributes to better fire-safety decisions, safer spacecraft designs, and ultimately the protection of astronauts. This becomes especially important as humans prepare for longer missions to the Moon and Mars, where the planned habitats will use higher oxygen levels and where emergencies are much harder to handle.

What makes our approach different is the combination of AI and 3D visualization. We didn’t want to build just another chatbot or research database. We wanted to bring the research to life, and to be honest about its limits: when NASA’s data doesn’t cover a situation, such as fire at Moon gravity, the platform says so instead of guessing.

During development, we considered the particular challenges of fire in microgravity, including flame behavior, oxygen concentration, airflow, fire detection and suppression, while keeping the platform accessible without losing the scientific value of the information.

Technologies used:

  • Programming language: Python
  • AI architecture: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
  • AI model/API: Claude API
  • Data: NASA Physical Science Informatics (PSI) database and NASA technical reports (NTRS)
  • Core approach: AI-powered research retrieval and interactive 3D visualization
